title: an ordinary computed property access on a plain object stays an ordinary TypeScript operation
notes: The over-correction guard for the whole computed-member family. Recognizing `x["name"]` as a member access must not turn every element access into a compiler-owned call: `table["alpha"]` on a plain object is an ordinary property read, and so is `table[key]` through a binding. This repository has shipped six over-corrections; a corpus that only pins refusals invites the seventh. The non-literal key is deliberate — a computed key that names no statically known member is not a selection at all, and nothing in the recognizers may claim it.
